ai.description: *Dendrelaphis ashoki* (Colubridae) reaches 1.2 m. It is bronze-brown dorsally with a distinct black eye-stripe and a bright yellow ventrolateral stripe. It lacks the blue neck-patch of similar species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dendrelaphis ashoki* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous black stripe running through the eye that terminates abruptly before reaching the neck.
ai.habitat: *Dendrelaphis ashoki* inhabits the evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high elevations ranging from 800 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Dendrelaphis ashoki* is a diurnal snake that actively hunts for prey, such as frogs and lizards, primarily within the canopy and shrub layers of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis ashoki* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dendrelaphis ashoki* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
